speaker: Teacher (śrāddha-rule announced)
question: What is proclaimed?
premises: atha śrāddhavidhiḥ śrīmatṣaḍardhokto nigadyate — now the śrāddha-rule told in the Ṣaḍardha is proclaimed: canon named, rite announced.
inference: Charter: the Ṣaḍardha śrāddha-rule.
uncertainties: Ṣaḍardha text-name as printed — flagged lightly.

speaker: Teacher (Siddhātantra hint)
question: Where hinted, and for whom?
premises: siddhātantre sūcito 'sau mūrtiyāganirūpaṇe — in the Siddhātantra hinted, in the image-sacrifice exposition.
antyeṣṭyā suviśuddhānāmaśuddhānāṃ ca tadvidhiḥ — by funerary rite, for purified and impure, that is the rule: scope universal.
inference: Hinted in Siddhātantra; binding on pure and impure alike.

speaker: Teacher (memorial calendar)
question: When, and by whom?
premises: tryahe turye 'hni daśame māsi māsyādyavatsare — third day, fourth, tenth, month, first year: the memorial calendar.
varṣe varṣe sarvakālaṃ kāryastatsvaiḥ sa pūrvavat — year by year, at all times, by his own as before: kin perform, tradition bounds.
inference: Calendar and agents: kin, recurrently, as before.

speaker: Teacher (god, fire, food)
question: What are the opening acts?
premises: tatra prāgvadyajeddevaṃ homayedanale tathā — worship the god, offer in fire, as before.
tato naivedyameva prāggṛhītvā hastagocare — then the food-offering itself, first taken in hand's reach: food staged.
inference: Worship, fire, food-in-hand: the opening sequence.

speaker: Teacher (food-śakti visualized)
question: What is visualized?
premises: gururannamayīṃ śaktiṃ vṛṃhikāṃ vīryarūpiṇīm — the guru: the food-made, growing, potent-formed śakti.
dhyātvā tayā samāviṣṭaṃ taṃ sādhyaṃ cintayetsudhīḥ — meditated; by her pervaded: that target let the wise visualize.
inference: Food embodied as growing potent śakti; the target seen pervaded by her.

speaker: Teacher (fettered part offered)
question: What is offered, and what results?
premises: tato 'sya yaḥ pāśavo 'ṃśo bhogyarūpastamarpayet — then his fettered part, enjoyable-formed: offer it.
bhoktaryekātmabhāvena śiṣya itthaṃ śivībhavet — in the enjoyer through identity: thus the disciple becomes Śiva.
inference: Offer the fettered-enjoyable into the enjoyer; become Śiva.

speaker: Teacher (fetter-natures Śiva-made)
question: What is Śiva-made?
premises: bhogyatānyā tanurdeha iti pāśātmakā matāḥ — enjoyableness and the rest, body, frame: held fetter-natured.
śrāddhe mṛtoddhṛtāvantayāge teṣāṃ śivīkṛtiḥ — in śrāddha, corpse-uplifting, final sacrifice: their Śiva-making (dense junction flagged).
inference: Fetter-natures Śiva-made across three rites.

speaker: Teacher (whole rite for identity)
question: Why the whole rite if one suffices?
premises: ekenaiva vidhānena yadyapi syātkṛtārthatā — though fulfillment might come by one rite.
tathāpi tanmayībhāvasiddhyai sarvaṃ vidhiṃ caret — yet for identity-state accomplishment, perform the whole rite: fullness for identity.
inference: One rite may suffice; identity demands the whole.

speaker: Teacher (enjoyment-seeker's cause)
question: For whom abundance-rites?
premises: bubhukṣostu kriyābhyāsabhūmānau phalabhūmani hetu — for the enjoyment-seeker, in practice- and fruit-abundance as cause.
tato mṛtoddhāraśrāddhādyasmai samācaret — therefore corpse-uplifting, śrāddha and the rest perform for him.
inference: Abundance-seekers get the full funeral-śrāddha battery.

speaker: Teacher (the useless for the lit)
question: For whom is none of this useful?
premises: tattvajñānārkavidhvastadhvāntasya tu — for him whose darkness the knowledge-sun destroyed.
na ko 'pyayam antyeṣṭiśrāddhavidhyādirupayogī kadācana — none of this, funerary-śrāddha-rule and the rest, is ever of use.
inference: The lit need no funeral apparatus — ever.

speaker: Teacher (unity-day festival)
question: What festival for the lineage?
premises: teṣāṃ tu guru tadvargavargyasabrahmacāriṇām — for them: guru, group, mates, fellow celibates, lineage-followers.
tatsantānajuṣāmaikyadinaṃ parvadinaṃ bhavet — the unity-day is a festival day: lineage time sanctified.
inference: Lineage unity-day as festival.

speaker: Teacher (awakening surge festivals)
question: When are festivals?
premises: yadāhi bodhasyodrekastadā parvāha pūraṇāt — when awakening surges, then — O festival day! — from fulfillment.
janmaikyadivasau tena parvaṇī bodhasiddhitaḥ — birth-day and unity-day are festivals through accomplished awakening.
inference: Surge-days are festival-days: awakening makes the calendar.

speaker: Teacher (putraka's nāḍī service)
question: How does the putraka help?
premises: putrako 'pi yadā kasmaicana syādupakārakaḥ — when the putraka may help someone.
tadā mātuḥ pituḥ śaktervāmadakṣāntarālagāḥ — then mother's, father's, śakti's left-right-interval channels (flow — verb carried to v14).
inference: The putraka's service: the three lines' channels.
uncertainties: verb gapped, carried to pravāhayet v14 — flagged.

speaker: Teacher (channels flow, food offered)
question: What is done with the channels?
premises: nāḍīḥ pravāhayeddevāyārpayeta niveditam — make the channels flow; to the deity offer the offered food (triple fusion).
śrīmadbharuṇatantre ca tacchivena nirūpitam — and in the Bharuṇa tantra that was set forth by Śiva: canon named.
inference: Flow the channels, feed the deity; Bharuṇa tantra warrants.

speaker: Teacher (timing and spontaneity)
question: How is timing handled?
premises: tadvāhakālāpekṣā ca kāryā tadrūpasiddhaye — regard for flowing-time observed for form-accomplishment.
svācchandyenātha tatsiddhiṃ vidhinā bhāvinā caret — then by spontaneity effect it through the forthcoming rite: timing then freedom.
inference: Observe flowing-time; then spontaneity through the coming rite.

speaker: Teacher (śrauta, not fettered)
question: What form in any śrāddha?
premises: yasya kasyāpi vā śrāddhe gurudevāgnitarpaṇam — in anyone's śrāddha, guru-deity-fire libation.
sacakreṣṭi bhavecchrauto — with wheel-sacrifice, should be śrauta (Vedic-form).
natu syātpāśavo vidhiḥ — but no fettered rite should there be.
inference: Śrauta-form libation; fettered rite excluded.

speaker: Teacher (broken bell)
question: Who is worthless?
premises: śrīmaukuṭe tathā coktaṃ — so said in the Maukuṭa (Makuṭāgama).
śivaśāstre sthito 'pi yaḥ pratyeti vaidike — established even in Śiva-teaching, who trusts the Vedic.
bhagnaghaṇṭāvanna sa kiṃcana — is like a broken bell: nothing at all.
inference: Vedic-trusters, even Śaiva-established, are broken bells.

speaker: Teacher (Rudrahood and pleasures)
question: What fruit?
premises: tathoktadevapūjādicakrayāgāntakarmaṇā — by the rite from stated worship to wheel-sacrifice.
rudratvametyasau janturbhogāndivyānsamaśnute — having reached Rudrahood, this creature fully enjoys divine pleasures.
inference: Full rite → Rudrahood → divine enjoyments.

speaker: Teacher (channel-course spoken)
question: What course is spoken?
premises: atha vacmaḥ sphuṭaṃ śrīmatsiddhaye nāḍicāraṇam — now we speak clearly: for accomplishment, the channel-course (authorial we).
yā vāhayitumiṣyeta nāḍī tāmeva bhāvayet — whichever channel one wishes flowing, that very one visualize.
inference: The nāḍī-course: visualize whichever channel you want flowing.

speaker: Teacher (visualized channel flows)
question: How does it flow?
premises: bhāvanātanmayībhāve sā nāḍī vahati sphuṭam — in visualization-identity that channel clearly flows.
yadvā vāhayituṃ yeṣṭā tadaṅgaṃ tena pāṇinā — or to flow whichever desired: that limb, with that hand (the pressing hand readied).
inference: Identity makes it flow; limb and hand readied for pressing.

speaker: Teacher (belly pressed, both states)
question: What does pressing do?
premises: āpīḍya kukṣiṃ namayetsā vahennāḍikā kṣaṇāt — pressing the belly, bend: it flows, the little channel, at once.
evaṃ śrāddhamukhenāpi bhogamokṣobhayasthitim — thus even by śrāddha: the state of both enjoyment and liberation.
inference: Belly-press, instant flow; śrāddha yields enjoyment-and-release.
uncertainties: kuryāt gapped (v22), object named here — flagged.

speaker: Teacher (Śiva said, guide uplifts)
question: Who uplifts, and how?
premises: kuryāditi śivenoktaṃ tatra tatra kṛpālunā — 'let him effect it,' by compassionate Śiva said here and there.
śaktipātodaye jantoryenopāyena daiśikaḥ — when śaktipāta has arisen, by whatever means the guide (subject of karoti v23).
inference: Compassionate Śiva's word; the guide acts post-śaktipāta by any means.

speaker: Teacher (God of gods uplifts)
question: Who is the uplifter?
premises: karotyuddharaṇaṃ tattannirvāṇāyāsya kalpate — he effects uplifting, and that avails for his nirvāṇa.
uddhartā devadevo hi sa cācintyaprabhāvakaḥ — for the uplifter is the God of gods, of inconceivable power.
inference: The guide's act avails because the Uplifter is supreme.

speaker: Teacher (door of initiation)
question: Through what door?
premises: upāyaṃ gurudīkṣādidvāramātreṇa saṃśrayet — resort to means merely through guru-initiation-and-rest as door.
uktaṃ śrīmanmataṅgākhye munipraśnādanantaram — told in the Mataṅga after the sage's question: canon and occasion.
inference: Initiation as mere door; Mataṅga after the sage's question.

speaker: Teacher (the sage's question)
question: What was asked?
premises: muktirvivekāttattvānāṃ — 'liberation from discrimination of the tattvas —
dīkṣāto yogato yadi caryāmātrātkathaṃ sā syāt — if from initiation, from yoga, how from mere conduct?'
ityataḥ samamuttaram — to this, thence, a fitting answer (the question posed; answer follows).
inference: The question: if liberation needs yoga/dīkṣā, how mere conduct?

speaker: Teacher (the laughing Lord)
question: What did the Lord answer?
premises: prahasyoce vibhuḥ — laughing, said the Lord.
kasmādbhrāntiste parameśituḥ — 'whence your delusion about the Supreme?'
sarvānugrāhakatvaṃ hi saṃsiddhaṃ dṛśyatāṃ kila — 'his all-gracing is established — look!'
inference: The laughing refutation: all-gracing is established fact.

speaker: Teacher (death-causes liberate)
question: How do death-causes liberate?
premises: prāptamṛtyorviṣavyādhiśastrādi kila kāraṇam — for the death-facing, poison, disease, weapons are the cause.
alpaṃ vā bahu vā tadvadanudhyā muktikāraṇam — small or great, that, so meditated, is a liberation-cause (dense junction flagged).
inference: Whatever kills, rightly meditated, liberates.

speaker: Teacher (outer marks employed)
question: How are outer marks used?
premises: muktyarthamupacaryante bāhyaliṅgānyamūni tu — for liberation these outer marks are employed.
iti jñātvā na sandeha itthaṃ kāryo vipaścitā — knowing thus, no doubt: so to be done by the wise.
inference: Outer marks as liberation-tools; doubtless performance.

speaker: Teacher (devotion and seal)
question: What if 'just this much' doubts?
premises: iyataiva kathaṃ muktiriti bhaktiṃ parāṃ śrayet — 'how liberation from just this much?' — resort to supreme devotion.
uktaḥ śrāddhavidhirbhrāntigarātaṅkavimardanaḥ — told is the śrāddha-rule, crusher of delusion-poison-dread: the seal.
inference: Answer to scruple: supreme devotion; the rule crushes delusion.
